renders.note: Why each committed render looks as it does; free-form, read by people. The values in manifest.json are the record, test_antibodies_data_provenance.py checks that these agree with them.
renders.method: World +z is the image's up and render_box_grid.py does not rotate a structure, so candidate directions were generated rather than guessed: 4000 points on the sphere, orthographic projection at 1728 x 972 with margin 1.02, scored by scale (px per angstrom), by the overlap of the two partners' silhouettes (Calpha discs of 3 angstrom), by how side-on the view is to the axis between the partners' centroids, and by how much of the interface (1SY6) or of the peptide (6TRO) a Calpha z-buffer leaves visible. Three well-separated directions per entry were draft-rendered (--draft, 864 x 486) and the choice was made by eye on those drafts and on crops of the contact. The scoring script was a scratch one and is not committed; the numbers below are its output. 2026-10-09.

hero.why: Re-chosen at the design review, 2026-10-09, to fill the frame. molrender fits its orthographic camera to the projected corners of the complex's axis-aligned bounding box about the box's centre (molrender blender/view.py, place_camera), not to the atoms, so a view with any z component also frames the box's top face, and on a tall complex that costs scale: the first choice, [-0.86, -0.24, 0.45], drew 1SY6 at 7.0 px per angstrom with its ink 0.26 of the frame's width and 0.77 of its height. A level view frames the box's height alone. Of the level views whose two partners overlap by at most 0.05 and which are at least 0.95 side-on, this one is 0.99 side-on and its production render (re-measured 2026-10-15 on the margin 1.06 render after the camera fix: the ink 694 x 918 px of 1728 x 972) measures 9.12 px per angstrom, the ink's height over the atoms' 100.6 angstrom extent in z, with the ink 0.40 of the width and 0.94 of the height (0.38 of the area, against 0.20): CD3 top left, held at the tip of the Fv, and the constant domains bottom right, the long axis leaning about 29 degrees from vertical.
hero.method: Scored with a framing model that reproduces molrender's fit (bounding box of the atoms plus 1 angstrom, its corners about its centre, margin 1.02, 1728 x 972); on the first choice it predicts 7.04 px per angstrom and an ink box of 0.28 x 0.77 of the frame, against 6.7 to 7.0 and 0.26 x 0.77 measured on that render. 2850 directions on a Fibonacci sphere (|z| at most 0.95); overlap from Calpha discs of 3 angstrom on a 1 angstrom grid, as a fraction of the smaller partner; side-on against the axis between the Fab's and CD3's centroids. Three level candidates were draft-rendered (864 x 486) and the choice made by eye on those and on crops of the contact. The scratch scripts are not committed; the scale of the earlier candidates below is this model's, not the atoms-only projection's 8.78 to 9.48.

candidates.verdict: The first choice. The contact reads, but the oblique view leaves the complex in 0.26 x 0.77 of the frame (measured on its render). Replaced.
As large, with CD3 top right; a little less side-on. Rejected on that margin.
The first choice's azimuth brought level: the same composition, larger, but CD3 overlaps the Fv in projection and the two partners merge. Rejected.

hero.limits: 1SY6 stands along world z with CD3 on top and the renderer has no roll, so every side-on view is a portrait object in the 16:9 frame: a level view fills its height, and the steepest lean a side-on view allows, about 30 degrees, takes it to about 0.4 of the width. The non-square hero is never cropped (spec 6.2).

mage-a4-pmhc-tcr.why: The peptide runs along the groove between the two alpha helices of the HLA-A*02:01 heavy chain and 64 per cent of its atoms are unobscured (a Calpha z-buffer); the complex's bounding box fills 77 per cent of the frame area, the most of the three (54 per cent for the first candidate), and the view is side-on to the pMHC-TCR axis (1.00).

candidates.verdict: The peptide is clear but the complex's bounding box fills only 54 per cent of the frame area. Rejected.
The peptide sits half behind the front helix. Rejected.

mage-a4-pmhc-tcr.limits: The PDB frame puts the TCR below the pMHC (lower z) and the picture cannot be rolled, so the TCR is lower right, the opposite of the textbook picture. Views with the TCR above left 7 to 30 per cent of the peptide visible and were near end-on.

radii.why: The panel overrides the plate's 0.4 and 0.22 (the carbon plates' values). The peptide is about 28 angstrom long in a frame about 127 angstrom wide, and at 0.4 and 0.22 its sticks and spheres were thin; both settings were rendered at the production tier and compared, and 0.6 and 0.3 read clearly. To restore the plate's values, delete the two panel keys and re-render with --force (about 2.5 minutes).
